nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--6853a1.title: Tyrosine trends the opposite way and isoleucine shows no pattern

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--7d46eb.gist: In soil samples alone, communities with more complete leucine-making pathways still had lower leucine levels in their metabolite data; arginine's link weakened but stayed negative. Most amino acids leaned negative, though the report also gives tyrosine leaning the opposite way.
nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--7d46eb.title: Leucine link holds in soil-only samples; arginine link weakens

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--dcef62.gist: In these environmental community samples, most of 13 amino-acid synthesis pathways were less complete where more of that amino acid was present, with leucine and arginine clearest. The report gives both results: tyrosine ran the opposite way.
nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--dcef62.title: Most pathways are less complete where their amino acid is abundant

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--fb740b.gist: In these soil and freshwater communities, the main axis of difference was carbon-use pathways, with soil communities appearing more complete in them. Amino acid pathways loaded more strongly on a second axis, which separated samples within the soil group.

nmdc_context_audit--10a5a668.gist: Among the lakehouse resources labeled NMDC, the genome (MAG) and NEON sets were committed most recently, on 2026-07-02, while the NCBI biosamples resource was the stalest, last committed on 2026-03-09, about 4 months old.

nmdc_context_audit--7809faa5.gist: Searching the lakehouse for "nmdc" returns 20 database names, yet they boil down to a much smaller set of real, maintained resources of differing origin, so the shared label says little about what each one actually is.

nmdc_context_audit--99bbd8c1.gist: In the KBase Data Lakehouse, the catalog's tables carry no comments and its databases have empty properties fields, so the catalog itself holds no human-readable description of what the NMDC-labelled resources contain.

nmdc_context_audit--b3940fd4.gist: Roughly half the databases in the lakehouse's nmdc tenant are external data copied in, such as an NCBI BioSample harvest and a Pfam protein-family list. The NMDC-specific databases sit under a different tenant, so browsing nmdc does not show them.

nmdc_context_audit--d8ef5d8f.gist: In the lakehouse, the genuine NMDC biosample collection is small, while the NCBI biosample mirror hosted beside it is about 3,000 times larger, and nothing in the database names signals the difference.

pangenome_openness--0e2125d9.gist: In these pangenomes, a species' pangenome openness showed no detectable relationship with the environment effect on its gene content. The report gives a parallel result for the phylogeny effect, which also showed no detectable relationship.

pangenome_openness--737ca282.gist: How open a species' pangenome is (how readily it gains new genes) showed no detectable relationship with the phylogeny effect, the share of variation tied to evolutionary relatedness. The report gives the same null result for the environment effect.

paperblast_explorer--15fe9e7d.gist: In a text-mined literature database, the 100 most-studied bacteria account for 44.3% of bacterial papers. Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, Escherichia coli K-12 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 lead, while environmental and non-pathogenic bacteria are far less studied.

paperblast_explorer--3dc1e920.gist: In a text-mined literature database of genes, about two-thirds of genes are linked to just one paper, while a small fraction of genes, led by human genes such as p53, account for over half of all gene-paper links.

paperblast_explorer--415e8345.gist: Humans alone account for 46.7% of gene-paper records in PaperBLAST, and the five leading organisms (human, mouse, rat, Arabidopsis, fruit fly) together hold most of them. The great majority of organisms with any literature share only a sliver.

paperblast_explorer--9d3f88b4.gist: Grouping proteins into families by sequence similarity, 9.2% of families have no text-mined paper for any member, and many more have just one. Some multi-member families have no detectable literature at all, suggesting much protein sequence space is little studied.

pathway_capability_dependency--250e9510.gist: In growth-related pathways of seven model bacteria, the largest group was pathways that are fully encoded yet whose genes showed no fitness defects under standard lab conditions, outnumbering pathways whose genes proved important for growth.

pathway_capability_dependency--4df15631.gist: Grouping genomes by which metabolic pathways they carry, in species with many sequenced genomes, gave a typical four metabolic ecotypes per species. This suggests a species often contains a few distinct metabolic types rather than one uniform profile.

pathway_capability_dependency--61e28c8b.gist: When fitness effects were separated by condition type (nitrogen source, carbon source, stress and others), all 66 latent-capability pathway-organism pairs became important for fitness under at least one condition type, suggesting their importance depends on the conditions tested.

pathway_capability_dependency--84c4b29b.gist: Across 2,810 species with at least 10 genomes, species whose genomes differ more in which metabolic pathways they carry also tend to have more open pangenomes. The link grows stronger once the number of sequenced genomes is accounted for.

pathway_capability_dependency--f655b856.gist: The report planned to test whether groups of genomes with different metabolic capabilities within a species occupy broader or narrower environmental ranges, using satellite-derived environment data. That analysis was not run, so the question remains open.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--45e0cc45.gist: Plant-growth genes sat in the variable accessory part of bacterial genomes less often than genes overall, at 29.7% versus the genome-wide share. This suggests they are mostly carried in the core genome, consistent with vertical inheritance.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--6ad3c804.gist: A complete tryptophan-making pathway went with carrying ipdC, a plant-hormone gene, in non-soil bacterial species. In soil and rhizosphere species the association reversed: tryptophan-complete species were less likely to carry it, hinting at an environment-specific pattern.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--6ef7f988.gist: The gene for ACC deaminase, a plant-stress enzyme, is about 7× more common in soil and rhizosphere bacterial species than in other environments. The enrichment persists when bacterial phylum is accounted for and is stronger when only root-associated genomes are counted.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--7e9e60f9.gist: Across the genomes analysed, the nitrogen-fixation gene nifH turned up together with the cyanide-production gene hcnC and the phosphate-solubilisation gene pqqC less often than expected, while showing no clear link to the auxin gene ipdC. Nitrogen fixers seem to differ from other plant-growth-promoting gene carriers.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--ac2bd4ee.gist: A pathway chosen as a negative control, tyrosine synthesis, predicted which species carry ipdC about as strongly as tryptophan synthesis did. The control test was inconclusive about whether the tryptophan link to ipdC is specific.

phage_defense_arsenal--40a9f7b2.gist: Among the bacterial defense systems compared, Type II restriction-modification and the Gabija anti-phage system showed the strongest tendency to occur in the same species, appearing together in 2,429 species, far more often than chance pairing would produce.

phage_defense_arsenal--47aaf35d.gist: Among the 7,323 bacterial species with at least five sequenced genomes, species with more anti-phage defense systems also tend to have more predicted prophage clusters. The link weakens but persists after accounting for genome size and phylum, suggesting the two go together in these species.

phage_defense_arsenal--707f57b3.gist: In a survey of anti-phage defense genes across bacterial genomes, one protein-domain annotation table showed no detectable hits for Cas1, a classic CRISPR marker, while a second annotation source reported ~25K hits. That table therefore under-detects classical defense markers.

phage_defense_arsenal--8c6a7f5f.gist: Among the anti-phage defense system pairs tested across bacterial species, CRISPR-Cas and CBASS were the only pair with no detectable tendency to occur together. CBASS appeared essentially independent of CRISPR-Cas, even though CRISPR-Cas is far more common.
phage_defense_arsenal--8c6a7f5f.title: CRISPR-Cas and CBASS are the one defense pair with no co-occurrence pattern

phb_granule_ecology--0215baea.gist: In these genomes, no PHB (a carbon-storage polymer) production genes were reported for Campylobacterota, Gemmatimonadota, Nanoarchaeota or Marinisomatota, and Patescibacteria was near zero at 0.4%, suggesting the pathway is rare or absent in these major lineages.

phb_granule_ecology--1de7b86b.gist: In this survey of bacterial and archaeal species, the PHB-making gene phaC was common in Pseudomonadota (60.9%) but much rarer in lineages such as Actinomycetota and Desulfobacterota, so carrying it varies widely by phylum.

phb_granule_ecology--589de302.gist: The PHB storage-polymer gene phaC was more common in species from highly variable environments than stable ones within every genome-size group, small to large. The difference was greatest in smaller genomes and smallest, 1.4x, in the largest.

phb_granule_ecology--5e2bc604.gist: The PHB-synthesis gene phaC is carried by roughly 44.0% of plant-associated species but only a few percent of animal-associated species, with soil and wastewater high and human-associated, marine and freshwater species falling in between, across species grouped by primary environment.

phb_granule_ecology--ef20cc78.gist: The report asks whether genomes carrying the PHB carbon-storage pathway also belong to species living in a wider range of environments, as a feast-and-famine lifestyle would predict. The test is inconclusive: genome size accounts for the apparent link, so it gives no independent support.

phb_granule_ecology--f9008fe7.gist: Among the 311 species whose phaC (a key gene for making the carbon-storage polymer PHB) sits oddly against their family tree, 60.1% carry it in the accessory genome, nearly double the rate across phaC-carrying species generally. This suggests horizontal acquisition.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--223dadd3.gist: Comparing plant-associated bacterial genomes by shuffling labels within each genus, only nitrogen fixation, ACC deaminase (an enzyme that breaks down ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene) and the type III secretion system stayed linked to plant association, out of 15 testable markers.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--64143b61.gist: Of the plant-associated species with enough host data to test, two Xanthomonas species split by host across subclades: X. campestris in one subclade comes almost entirely from Brassica, and X. vasicola in another mostly from maize.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--8106ac12.gist: Nearly all (96%) of the top plant-enriched gene families stayed clearly more common in plant-associated bacterial genomes after accounting for bacterial phylum and genome size, suggesting the plant association is not simply a taxonomy or genome-size effect.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--de6d574e.gist: In plant-associated microbial genomes, the large difference between plant compartments fell to a small fraction of its original size once the three most dominant species per compartment were left out, though some difference remained. The original signal was largely driven by a few species.
plant_microbiome_ecotypes--de6d574e.title: Compartment difference shrank sharply once a few dominant species were removed

prophage_amr_comobilization--02e63b0a.gist: Across 4,770 species, those with a higher density of prophage (integrated virus) markers in their genomes also tended to carry a broader range of antibiotic-resistance genes, and the pattern held after accounting for how many genomes each species had.

prophage_amr_comobilization--3eb68b95.gist: Whether antibiotic-resistance genes lying near prophages (viral DNA integrated in bacterial genomes) differ in fitness cost from other resistance genes was not tested, so the question stays open for future work.

prophage_amr_comobilization--4cead8a0.gist: Antibiotic-resistance genes sitting within 10 genes of a prophage (integrated virus) marker were only slightly more often accessory, meaning absent from some strains, than more distant ones: about two-thirds in both groups, 67.6% against a marginally lower share.

prophage_amr_comobilization--7802d299.gist: In the 100 species carrying the most antibiotic-resistance genes, over half (55.7%) of resistance gene copies sit on the same DNA contigs as prophage marker genes, but many are far down the contig from the nearest marker in gene order.

prophage_amr_comobilization--f3c69b78.gist: Across the full pangenome inventory, just over half of species (52.9%) carry markers for both antibiotic-resistance genes and prophages (integrated viruses), so the two are widespread together across species. Prophage markers were mostly accessory genes.

prophage_ecology--3c13d0b7.gist: Testing viral terminase (DNA-packaging gene) lineages against environment types turned up no lineage with a clear environment preference beyond what the host bacteria's family tree already predicts. The analysis ran and found nothing, so lineage-level adaptation to environment is not apparent here.

prophage_ecology--967ce72a.gist: Using bacterial genus matches to infer prophage content across 6,365 NMDC metagenomic samples, the analysis found 57 correlations between prophage gene modules and abiotic variables such as pH, suggesting that prophage module patterns vary with environmental chemistry in these samples.

prophage_ecology--9f2125cc.gist: In the analyzed bacterial genomes, differences in prophage (integrated virus) gene module composition were associated most strongly with genome size group, less with the environment a genome came from, and least with family-level relatedness.

prophage_ecology--d880eadf.gist: Prophage-associated genes turned up in every bacterial species surveyed. Packaging, lysis and lysogeny-control modules are found in essentially all species, while head, tail and anti-defense modules vary, and 34.9% of species carry all seven modules.

prophage_ecology--fc67e694.gist: Across bacterial species, prophage tail, head-assembly and anti-defense gene modules were over-represented in human-associated species compared with null expectations, while anti-defense modules were under-represented in freshwater and animal-associated species.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--0211e0cd.gist: Differences in which carbon sources free-living species can use carry real ecological signal. Carbon-use profiles alone did not separate fine-grained environment types, so this test was inconclusive for telling those environments apart.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.gist: Predicted rhamnose and fucose pathways were more often complete in Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes (66.8%) than in the P. fluorescens group. The comparison was inconclusive, so it cannot settle whether the gap is real.
pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.title: Rhamnose and fucose pathways appear more complete in P. aeruginosa, but inconclusively

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--9c42f41a.gist: In these genomes, the Pseudomonas aeruginosa group is predicted to have lost nearly all plant-derived sugar breakdown pathways that the P. fluorescens/putida group retains. The two groups differ in 43 of the carbon pathways tested.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--a6ba828d.gist: Predicted pathways for using xylose, arabinose and myo-inositol are entirely absent in the P. aeruginosa group, but partly complete in the P. fluorescens group (up to 74.4% for xylose). Pathways for ribose, galacturonate, mannitol and sorbitol are also much less complete.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--cbe7e256.gist: A machine-learning classifier could tell, better than chance, whether a Pseudomonas species came from soil, freshwater, plant surfaces or the rhizosphere using only its carbon-use pathways. This suggests these pathways carry some ecological signal across 51 species.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--eb1d58ae.gist: Across 54 free-living and plant-associated Pseudomonas species, the mix of carbon-use pathways tracked where the strains were isolated: species from the same environment had more similar pathway profiles than species from different environments, suggesting carbon metabolism carries an ecological signal.

respiratory_chain_wiring--6d65c6de.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, the respiratory chain is used differently depending on the carbon source: quinate growth needs only Complex I, acetate needs several components, and glucose needs none in particular. The report describes distinct configurations, not a gradient.

respiratory_chain_wiring--7d7534df.gist: In Acinetobacter ADP1 grown under standard conditions, the three NADH-oxidizing respiratory enzymes (Complex I, NDH-2 and ACIAD3522) are all present at protein levels close to the genome median, suggesting respiratory wiring is set by metabolism rather than gene switching.

respiratory_chain_wiring--d117b49e.gist: In Acinetobacter ADP1, a single-subunit enzyme that oxidizes NADH without pumping protons (ACIAD3522) was lethal to lose when cells grew on acetate, but losing it did not hurt growth on quinate or glucose, where growth ratios were 1.39.

respiratory_chain_wiring--e16ee45a.gist: In Acinetobacter ADP1, growth on quinate depends more on Complex I than growth on glucose or acetate does, even though quinate yields fewer NADH per carbon atom (0.57). The report proposes a sudden NADH burst from ring cleavage that outpaces the alternative enzyme.

respiratory_chain_wiring--fcdd6421.gist: Across 14 bacterial species, those with a validated alternative NADH dehydrogenase (NDH-2) showed larger, not smaller, Complex I growth deficits on aromatic compounds, opposite to the compensation idea. The comparison was inconclusive, so the idea was not supported.

snipe_defense_system--5727ec31.gist: A survey of bacterial and archaeal pangenomes found the SNIPE phage-defense domain DUF4041 across 33 phyla, a far wider spread than the original paper's report of homologues. This suggests the domain is common across prokaryotic lineages.

snipe_defense_system--69396dc3.gist: In E. coli K-12 gene-knockout screens, losing the transporter genes manX, manY or manZ caused very severe growth defects in only four conditions each, and growth was affected far less in most other conditions tested.

snipe_defense_system--792b9ec1.gist: In Klebsiella, the PhageFoundry collection has ManYZ sugar-transport annotations, including 28 ManZ proteins, but only genome annotations and no gene-knockout fitness data. Whether SNIPE and ManYZ interact in Klebsiella is therefore unmeasured; the analysis was not possible with these data.

snipe_defense_system--a878d018.gist: Protein-family lookups for the E. coli SNIPE defence protein show its nuclease domain belongs to a family named Mug113 (PF13455), not the canonical GIY-YIG family PF01541. Both families sit in the same broader GIY-YIG group.

soil_frontier_genomics--0fa73728.gist: Models using climate and soil, geochemical, or industrial measurements to predict functional gene counts in soils worldwide each did worse on held-out samples than guessing the average. The comparison was inconclusive: it could not settle whether gene counts are predictable from these measurements.

soil_frontier_genomics--25df967c.gist: Soil areas flagged as genomic frontiers, where public genome coverage is thin, were more alkaline than well-mapped areas, with a +0.8 pH unit gap in mean pH. This suggests alkaline soil microbiomes are under-represented in public genome collections.

soil_frontier_genomics--2ab586c6.gist: In this soil survey, forest and cropland soils scored highest on the genomic discovery index, a combined measure of sampling gap and richness, while grassland and wetland soils scored about half as high. The index flags where soil microbes may be least characterized.

soil_frontier_genomics--a002c998.gist: Soils with low and high clay content showed no clear difference in how well gene counts could be predicted from soil measurements. The comparison was inconclusive.
soil_frontier_genomics--a002c998.title: Clay shield test finds no clear difference between low-clay and high-clay soils

soil_metal_functional_genomics--129a64ad.gist: In soil samples, many gene functional categories were associated with levels of nine metals. Chromium and lead gave the strongest signals, and the top hits were mostly transporter genes and genes for building cell components.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--129a64ad.title: Many gene-function links to metals in soils, strongest for chromium and lead

soil_metal_functional_genomics--2a80fc76.gist: In soil samples matched to nearby genomes, gene categories for cell division and nucleotide transport tracked higher copper, while energy-production categories tracked lower copper. This suggests an energy trade-off under copper stress.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--2a80fc76.title: Copper-linked gene categories suggest an energy trade-off in soils

soil_metal_functional_genomics--aaafa6a8.gist: For soil microbial communities, the report gives no figure for how much of the variation in gene-function profiles metal concentrations explain on their own, before differences between studies are removed. That number is missing, so the overall strength of the metal signal remains unquantified.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--becb7d4e.gist: When metal concentrations were compared with gene-function profiles separately in soil, marine and wastewater samples, the associations looked different in each environment. This suggests environment-specific patterns of association rather than one shared resistance programme across all three.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--becb7d4e.title: Metal–gene-function associations differ among soil, marine and wastewater environments

soil_metal_functional_genomics--e27860e8.gist: Across soil samples, 2,355 associations link metal levels to gene functional categories, but the report has not yet checked how strong each association is, so it is unclear how many reflect large versus small biological differences.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--e27860e8.title: Strength of each metal–gene-function association not yet reported

soil_metal_functional_genomics--fd9b94cc.gist: In soil samples, metal concentrations explained 80% of the variation in community gene-function profiles once differences between sampling projects were set aside. This suggests metal levels track shifts in the functional makeup of soil microbial communities.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--fd9b94cc.title: Metals explain most remaining community gene-function variation after removing project differences

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--44ad24db.gist: Among genomes assembled from metagenomes, those with a glycosyltransferase (GT2) gene near a type IV secretion system carried 11× more metal resistance genes than other genomes, suggesting a possible link between GT2 neighbourhoods and metal resistance.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--5d73bfde.gist: In these genomes, a mobile-element search found no detectable plasmid-borne carbohydrate-active enzyme genes, while genomes with type IV secretion machinery had 10× higher mobile-element density, a pattern consistent with chromosomal or integrative transfer.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--91e33b0b.gist: In these genomes, 92 families of carbohydrate-active enzymes (enzymes that build and modify sugars) sit unusually often near type IV secretion genes, a system linked to DNA transfer. The GT2 sugar-attaching family stands out most strongly.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--a2b33180.gist: A gene tree of GT2 sugar-building enzymes from environmental genomes contained 32 high-confidence gene transfers between distant bacterial phyla. The strongest one spans 8 phyla, suggesting these enzymes have moved between unrelated bacterial groups.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--a744bbc9.gist: Genes for type IV secretion and conjugation machinery, a set of proteins linked to DNA transfer between cells, were found in 21.8% of high-quality genomes reconstructed from environmental samples, so this machinery appears widespread across them.

truly_dark_genes--8c818410.gist: Among genes with strong growth effects, genes that stay unannotated after reannotation were not enriched in stress conditions. They turned up less often there than genes reannotation could name, and more in nutrient, mixed-community and iron conditions, hinting at metabolic or community roles.

truly_dark_genes--92c362cf.gist: Among the 39,532 Fitness Browser dark genes that have pangenome links, re-annotating with a newer tool reclassified 83.7%. That left a smaller core that both the original and the new annotation still call hypothetical proteins.

truly_dark_genes--947aec4f.gist: Genes that stay unexplained even after re-annotation tend to be shorter, less often in the core genome, and far less likely to have orthologs than genes that re-annotation could name. They are typically found in just one organism, suggesting a narrowly distributed set.

truly_dark_genes--ba47a194.gist: Among genes that stay unannotated even after re-annotation, only 3.8% are completely dark. Most carry at least a sequence identifier, and many show a fitness or essentiality signal without any functional description.

truly_dark_genes--d1b84273.gist: Genes that stay unexplained after modern re-annotation are concentrated in particular organisms: two Methanococcus archaeal strains hold 55% of them. Dark genes resisting re-annotation also vary widely among organisms, with archaea at the high end, suggesting poor annotation coverage of archaea.

webofmicrobes_explorer--6149b49e.gist: Linking Web of Microbes metabolites to predicted bacterial pathways by name did not work, because pathway labels are internal IDs that lack simple metabolite names. This is an unperformed analysis; a lookup table of each pathway's substrates and products is needed.
webofmicrobes_explorer--6149b49e.title: Direct metabolite-name matching to pathway predictions failed

webofmicrobes_explorer--ab7e4ba4.gist: In the archived 2018 Web of Microbes export, no organism has a 'Decreased' (consumption) entry, and all 742 'D' observations belong to the control. The analysis ran and found none, though the newer version may contain consumption data.

webofmicrobes_explorer--f572a74d.gist: In the Web of Microbes metabolite data, only 26.8% of identified compounds match a reference growth-model compound by exact name. Many others match by molecular formula alone, which gives only candidate sets of possible compounds, and some have no match.
